title: Can you operate a workflow safely?

questions.prompt: A job only checks out code and runs tests. Which built-in token permission is the better starting point?
questions.explanation: A test job normally needs to read repository contents but does not need broad write access.

questions.prompt: Which values or objects should a workflow treat as potentially untrusted? Select all that apply.

options.label: Code from a forked pull request
An artifact produced by another trust context
A fixed string written directly by the workflow author

questions.explanation: User-controlled text, forked code, and transferred files can carry attacker input. A fixed workflow literal does not have the same external origin.

questions.prompt: How should a workflow safely pass a pull request title to a command?

options.label: Store it in an environment variable and pass the quoted value as data
Insert the expression directly into shell source
Grant contents: write before using the title

questions.explanation: Separating untrusted text from shell source reduces the chance that punctuation in the value becomes executable syntax.

questions.prompt: Order the layers to inspect when a workflow should update an external service.

options.label: Confirm that a workflow run exists
Confirm that the relevant job scheduled
Inspect the command or action result

questions.explanation: Each layer depends on the prior one, while a successful step still does not prove the external system changed correctly.

questions.prompt: A workflow has a test job and a release job. Explain how you would apply least privilege to their built-in tokens.
questions.rubric: Credit answers that give the test job only read access or no unnecessary token rights, place release write permission only on the release job, and avoid granting broad workflow-wide rights merely for convenience.
questions.reference_answer: Set minimal workflow defaults, such as contents: read or permissions: {}. Keep the test job read-only. Add only the specific write permission needed for publishing to the release job, so a compromised test step cannot use release authority.
questions.explanation: Job-scoped permission limits keep elevated authority out of jobs that do not need it.

questions.prompt: Which practices make failures easier to diagnose? Select all that apply.

options.label: Give important jobs and steps descriptive names
Grant broad token rights so permission errors disappear

questions.explanation: Names, time limits, summaries, and reports expose useful evidence. Broad permissions hide design mistakes and increase risk.

questions.prompt: A test job can start with {{read-permission}}. Treat {{outside-values}} as untrusted data, and begin debugging by checking {{run-layer}} before inspecting later layers.

options.label: pull request titles and forked code

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits the test token, external values stay data rather than shell source, and debugging starts by confirming a run exists.
